description: Allowlist for the shipped-sources validity gate (packages/testing-framework/src/multilingual/shipped-sources-validity.test.ts). Each entry is a hyperscript source we ship that hyperfixi parses in the recovers-with-errors state (ok:true with a non-empty errors array). A NEW such source outside this list, or an allowlisted key that becomes clean, both fail the gate. Shrink this list as fixes land.
note: The `key` is file::sha1(source)[0:10], so it CHANGES when the source is edited — a fix cannot silently keep its allowlist cover, it drops off and the stale-entry test demands removal. `upstream` records the real hyperscript.org verdict, which is what distinguishes a malformed example (upstream also rejects) from a hyperfixi parser defect (upstream accepts). Three of the original four entries were cleared by the `then`-as-command-separator work: native-dialog and infinite-scroll by the parser fix (parseIfCommand's branch loops dropped BOTH the `then` separator and `--` comments, which every sibling body loop already handled), and fetch-data by deleting its `log 'typeof it:', (typeof it)` line — `typeof` is JavaScript, not a hyperscript operator. 2026-08-31: FOUR entries added at once when the parser learned to REPORT discarded input (previously these five parsed ok:true in total silence). None is a new defect; all five are pre-existing losses that had no channel to surface through. recipes.html is the one upstream accepts.
infiniteScrollFollowUp:
The handoff's guess that infinite-scroll.html also had a genuinely missing `end` was WRONG — its `end`s were balanced all along, and the whole hyperfixi error was the comment-in-if-body defect. Upstream still rejects it ("Expected 'end' but found 'on'", "Unexpected Token : {") over the multi-line `make a
  • …
    • ` element literal with `#{}` interpolation, which upstream does not support in that form. So we are now MORE permissive than upstream on that file. That laxness divergence is real but out of this gate's scope — the gate tracks hyperfixi's recovered state only.

allowedRecovered.error: Expected property name after '.' - malformed member access
allowedRecovered.upstream: You must parenthesize math operations with different operators
allowedRecovered.reason: MIXED — both engines reject, but for unrelated reasons, so this is two bugs in one file. Upstream's is an authoring bug with a known fix: `set midpoint to box.top + box.height / 2` mixes `+` and `/` without parens, which hyperscript forbids (x2 occurrences); `box.top + (box.height / 2)` is the fix. Hyperfixi's complaint is DIFFERENT ('malformed member access') and survives that fix, so it is likely a second parser-side gap around the `add { prop: value; }` inline-style syntax — confirm before editing the example.

allowedRecovered.error: Discarded input the parser could not place: 'in the next <div/> when its textContent contains my value'
allowedRecovered.reason: HYPERFIXI PARSER DEFECT, and the clearest one this gate has surfaced. `show <blockquote/> in the next <div/> when <cond>` parses on hyperscript.org; we keep the `show` and silently discard BOTH the `in <scope>` qualifier and the `when` filter, so the shipped example shows every blockquote instead of filtering. Newly VISIBLE (not newly broken) — the drop predates the diagnostics that expose it.

allowedRecovered.error: Discarded input the parser could not place: 'item : last-child'
allowedRecovered.reason: MIXED, and the two engines disagree about WHY. Upstream rejects the `swap delete <target>` form outright (it wants `with`); we accept the form but mis-tokenize the pseudo-class, splitting `.item:last-child` at the `:` — the same colon-splitting class as the colon-event-names arc. Fixing the tokenizer would leave upstream's objection standing, so check whether `swap delete` is a hyperfixi extension before editing the example.

allowedRecovered.error: Discarded input the parser could not place: 'try'
allowedRecovered.reason: DOCS DEFECT, both engines. The example documents `try … catch error … end` as a command block; neither engine has that (upstream attaches `catch` to the handler, not to a `try`). We drop the `try` keyword, run its body, and discard the ENTIRE catch branch — so a docs example about error handling ships with its error handling silently removed.

allowedRecovered.error: Discarded input the parser could not place: '( me )'
allowedRecovered.reason: DOCS DEFECT / feature gap, both engines. `send profileUpdated({user: it})` passes an object literal as a call argument; upstream rejects the `{` and we drop the `formToJSON(me)` call arguments. The documented `send <event>(<detail>)` shape needs checking against what either engine actually supports before the example is rewritten.

localOnlyTrap: The walk is restricted to `git ls-files` (2026-08-31). It previously walked the working TREE, which is not a clean checkout: 10 untracked/ignored files under examples/experiments, examples/playground, examples/vite-plugin-multilingual, examples/vite-plugin-test and one docs/*.md were scored locally and never existed in CI (local denominator 183 vs CI's 173). That is unfixable from the allowlist — an entry for such a file fails in CI as STALE, and no entry fails locally as NEW. The sibling shipped-examples-execution gate had derived its corpus from git since #862 for exactly this reason; this gate was never brought into line, and the gap cost a CI round-trip on 2026-08-31 (a fifth allowlist entry, the Spanish `on click alternar .active on me`, came from a local-only file and had to be withdrawn).
